newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt under no pressure to buy wheat- traders.
newsitem.headline: Egypt under no pressure to buy wheat- traders.

text.p: Egypt is under no pressure to buy wheat but the intentions of its official commodities buyer are hard to gauge, Cairo-based grain traders said on Thursday.

European exporters had said they expected heavyweight buyer Egypt back into the world grain market soon to buy wheat for May and June but the traders told Reuters it was difficult to predict what Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC), would do.

"He's not under any pressure, in no hurry and has no definite reason to enter the market aggressively. He may or may not do so, but for sure he will play the game to his own benefit and good prices," one trader said.

The European traders say Egypt would soon buy 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of mainly U.S. wheat but Shakankiri told Reuters in February that after buying 400,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, he had grain to tide him over until July at least.
The official was unreachable for comment on Thursday.
"Egypt's stocks have not lessened but you never know with the GASC...they like to pounce on the market and get the prices they want," another trader said.
Shakankiri has in the past suprised the market with snap tenders and then ended up buying three or even four times the amount of wheat he asked for. --Miral Fahmy +202 578 3290/1
